findings.title: Blocked-address matching is case-sensitive and can be trivially bypassed
findings.body: `should_block?` compares the submitted value directly against the stored string. The signup path assigns `params[:email]` directly to `User#email`, so a row for `bad@spamclub.com` does not match a signup using `bad@SPAMCLUB.COM` (or other casing variants) on a case-sensitive database. This differs from the domain restrictions, which use a case-insensitive regexp, and allows a blocked address to register simply by changing case. Normalize both blocked-email records and values being checked with the application's canonical email normalization (for example `Email.downcase(...).strip`), and ensure lookup/indexing uses that normalized form.

findings.title: Match-count updates lose increments under concurrent validation
findings.body: The counter is updated with a read-modify-write sequence (`record.match_count += 1` followed by `save`). Two concurrent signup attempts for the same blocked address can both read the same count and save the same incremented value, causing one or more matches to be lost. Since this table explicitly records match statistics, use an atomic database update such as `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or locking/counter updates so concurrent attempts are counted correctly.
